# Gloomwater

A relaxed 3D fishing game (three.js). It ships as one self-contained page, `Gloomwater-Mossmere.html`:
open it in a browser to play.

## The one rule

**Edit `src/`, never `Gloomwater-Mossmere.html`.** The HTML is generated by `npm run build` from the files
in `src/`; any hand edit to it is overwritten by the next build. Commit the rebuilt HTML together with the
`src/` change that produced it.

## Files

| Path                                           | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Gloomwater-Mossmere.html`                     | The built game, the one file people play. Generated; do not edit.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `src/shell.html`                               | The page around the scripts: head, styles, the two small inline scripts, the loader. It holds three placeholders, `@@GW_INCLUDE:game.js@@`, `@@GW_INCLUDE:field-guide.html@@` and `@@GW_INCLUDE:spore-guide.html@@`. |
| `src/game.js`                                  | The `<script type="module">` body: three.js plus all game code, as one file. It comes from a minified bundle, so identifiers are short; it has been formatted with Prettier, nothing else.                           |
| `src/field-guide.html`, `src/spore-guide.html` | Two standalone documents the game opens. The page stores each as a JSON string inside a `<script type="application/json">` element; the build encodes them.                                                          |
| `tools/build.mjs`                              | Assembles `src/` into `Gloomwater-Mossmere.html`, squeezing the spacing and comments out of the game code on the way (whitespace only, via esbuild). Deterministic. Prints the size and SHA-256. `--readable` builds an unsqueezed copy for debugging.                                                                          |
| `tools/verify-equivalence.mjs`                 | Proves the built page is the same program as a committed one (see below).                                                                                                                                            |
| `tools/smoke.mjs`                              | Plays the opening of a new game in headless Chromium and fails on any console or page error.                                                                                                                         |
| `tools/scenarios.mjs`                          | Scenario tests: loads each save fixture, boots the built game in headless Chromium and drives it through `window.__gw`.                                                                                              |
| `tools/game-driver.mjs`                        | The browser driver the scenario tests and the fixture maker share.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `tools/fixtures/`                              | Real saves made by the game (`tools/make-fixtures.mjs`); its README says how each was made.                                                                                                                          |
| `docs/`                                        | Design notes.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## Build and test

Needs Node 22. `npm install` fetches the dev tools (Prettier, ESLint, esbuild, acorn).

```sh
npm run build    # src/ -> Gloomwater-Mossmere.html
npm test         # lint, build, then the smoke test: run this before every commit
npm run lint     # every identifier the game reads must be declared (catches patch typos in seconds)
npm run verify   # same program as another commit? See below
npm run scenarios # load each save fixture, play from it, check the scenarios (about five minutes)
npm run format   # Prettier on src/game.js and tools/
```

**The smoke test needs Playwright with Chromium.** Playwright is not a dependency of this repository; the
test loads it with `require("playwright")`, so a global install that Node can resolve works. It renders with
SwiftShader (software WebGL2), opens the page from a `file://` URL, starts a new game, picks a Wick, skips
the intro, taps through the opening tow, sails onto the Mossmere and makes one cast. It takes about a
minute. Google Fonts requests are answered with an empty stylesheet so the test never depends on the
network.

### Why the built page is squeezed

`src/game.js` is formatted so people can read and edit it, which costs about 1.8 MB of spacing. The build
prints it back without spacing or comments before it goes into the page (esbuild, whitespace only: no
syntax or name changes), so players get the smaller file and the source stays readable. The tests always
run against the squeezed page, the one people play.

To debug with readable code and line numbers, run `node tools/build.mjs --readable`. It writes
`Gloomwater-Mossmere.readable.html`, which is ignored by git. Never commit a readable build as
`Gloomwater-Mossmere.html`.

### Rules the build enforces

- `src/game.js` must not contain `</script`, `<!--` or `<script` anywhere, including strings, comments and
  template literals: the HTML parser would end or confuse the script element. Write `"<\/script"` or
  `"<" + "script"` instead. The build names the line and column.
- Each placeholder must appear exactly once in `src/shell.html`.
- All sources must be UTF-8 without a byte-order mark.

### What verify proves

`npm run verify -- --base <rev>` compares the built page with the one committed at `<rev>` (default `HEAD`):
the bytes outside the three script bodies are identical, the two JSON template bodies are byte-identical,
and the two module scripts are the same program. For the module it first tries a whitespace-only
comparison (esbuild `minifyWhitespace` on both sides); if that differs it compares the parsed ASTs
(acorn), ignoring positions and how literals are spelled, comparing comments, and tolerating one thing
only: a chain of one logical operator grouped differently, `a && (b && c)` versus `(a && b) && c`, which
Prettier rebalances and which always evaluates identically. It prints every tolerated difference.

### Formatting note

`src/game.js` is formatted with Prettier 3.3.3 using `.prettierrc` (`printWidth` 110), run until stable, so
`npm run format` changes nothing on a clean tree. The code maps in `docs/maps/` cite line numbers from a
single-pass copy of the same formatting: they are exact up to about line 58200 and up to 4 lines out after
that. Search by the anchor a map gives, not by its line number.

### Where this came from

The game used to exist only as a minified bundle that was patched by hand. `src/` was produced from that
bundle by formatting alone. `npm run verify -- --base 5a216a5` re-proves that the built page is the same
program as the last minified build.
